classification.difficultyReason: Interpret horizontal lines on the supplied cubic-shaped graph and distinguish heights outside, at and between the labelled extrema, counting tangency as one distinct solution.

content.prompt: The diagram below shows the graph of a function $y=f(x)$. Find the value(s) of $k$ such that $f(x)=k$ has

spec.description: Schematic cubic-shaped curve preserving the two labelled turning points, origin crossing, end directions and unticked axes. Bézier segments reproduce the supplied qualitative graph without asserting an equation.
spec.mathematics: Local maximum (-1,2), local minimum (1,-2); three monotone branches.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied graph features remain visible in the question.

answer.worked: The horizontal line $y=k$ meets the curve once when it lies below the local minimum or above the local maximum. Hence $k<-2$ or $k>2$.
At $k=2$ or $k=-2$, the horizontal line touches a turning point and meets another branch once. There are two distinct intersections, so $k=\pm2$.
A horizontal line strictly between the turning-point heights meets all three branches. Hence $-2<k<2$.
